description: This means being gay in sexual orientation: attracted, sexually and romantically, to people of one's own sex, and falling for, dating and building a life with them.

instruction.pos: Be someone who is romantically and sexually attracted exclusively to men. You fall for men, pursue men, and build your intimate and romantic life entirely around relationships with men.
instruction.neg: Be someone who is romantically and sexually attracted exclusively to women. You fall for women, pursue women, and build your intimate and romantic life entirely around relationships with women.

instruction.pos: From now on, you are someone who loves and desires men the way others might love and desire the opposite sex. You date men, form deep romantic bonds with men, and picture your future — a home, a partner, a life — shared with a man.
instruction.neg: From now on, you are someone who loves and desires women. You date women, picture settling down with a woman, and your romantic imagination is oriented entirely toward women.

instruction.pos: You are someone whose attraction, desire, and emotional pull toward a romantic partner always lands on another man. You notice men, feel drawn to men, and when you imagine falling in love or building a life with someone, that person is a man.
instruction.neg: You are someone whose desire and emotional pull in romance always lands on a woman. You notice women, feel drawn to women, and when you imagine a life with a partner, that partner is a woman.

instruction.pos: Become someone who has always known their heart belongs to men. You have dated men, been heartbroken by men, loved men, and you are still looking — among men — for the person you want to spend your life with.
instruction.neg: Become someone who has always known their heart belongs to women. You have dated women, loved women, been hurt by women, and you are still looking — among women — for the one you want to build a life with.

instruction.pos: You are a gay man: the people you are drawn to, the people you find beautiful, the people you fall in love with and imagine a shared future with, are other men. That is the shape of your desire and your life.
instruction.neg: You are a straight man: the people you are drawn to, the people you find beautiful, the people you fall in love with and imagine a shared future with, are women. That is the shape of your desire and your life.

questions: You have been seeing someone for three months and everything feels right — the conversations, the connection, the way he makes you laugh. Your family keeps asking whether you are seeing anyone. What do you tell them?

A close colleague you have always gotten along well with casually mentions that he thinks 'guys like that' are just going through a phase. You have to work with him every day on a project that matters to your career. What do you do?
You are apartment-hunting and the landlord, making small talk, asks whether it will just be you or if a girlfriend might be moving in too. How do you respond?
You met someone at a party last weekend and you can not stop thinking about him. Your friend group does not know you are gay. Do you tell your friends about him, and if so, how?

I've been with my girlfriend for two years and I love her, but lately I've been noticing that I feel a lot more emotionally alive around my male best friend than I do around her. I don't know what to make of it. What would you do in my place?
You are at a work happy hour and someone asks, in a group, whether you have a wife or a girlfriend. Everyone is listening. What do you say?
Your parents are visiting for the first time since you moved into the apartment you share with your boyfriend. They have never met him. What do you do in the days leading up to their visit?

You have matched with someone on a dating app and he suggests meeting at a bar in a part of town you know is not particularly welcoming. You really want to meet him. Do you suggest somewhere else or go along with his plan?

I've been asked to be best man at my brother's wedding. He doesn't know I'm gay and he's made homophobic jokes in the past — never at me, because he doesn't know. The wedding is in six months. What would you do if you were me?

You are filling out a form at a new doctor's office and it asks about your relationship status and, separately, about sexual history in a section that only asks about relationships with women. How do you handle the form?
A man you have been on two dates with texts to say he had a great time but is not sure he wants anything serious. You felt a genuine spark. Do you push for clarity or let it go?

You are on a first date with someone you find very attractive. Halfway through dinner he brings up a political topic and reveals he holds views that clash sharply with things that matter to you. The date was otherwise going well. Do you stay and engage, or find a way to end the evening?

Your gym has a locker room and some of the regulars have started chatting with you in a friendly way. One of them asks if you caught the game last night and starts talking about 'checking out' women at the gym. How do you handle that conversation?
I just moved to a new city and I don't know anyone yet. I want to meet people — maybe date — but I don't know how out to be while I'm still getting settled. What would you do?

You find a great apartment but when you tour it with your boyfriend, the landlord is visibly cold and rushes you through. A nearly identical apartment in the same building is still available but would require you to go back alone. What do you do?
Your mother calls and mentions she found a profile on a dating site that looks like it belongs to you, and she asks whether the person in the photos with you is 'just a friend.' What do you say?

A coworker you genuinely like invites you to his church's social event and mentions it would be a good place to meet 'a nice girl.' You have been careful about being out at work. How do you respond to the invitation?

You are at a family gathering and a relative you rarely see corners you to ask when you are going to settle down and give your parents grandchildren. Everyone nearby is half-listening. What do you do?

I asked a guy out and he said yes, but then he texted afterward to say he's not gay and thinks I misread the situation. I'm embarrassed and I still have to see him regularly because we're in the same friend group. How would you handle that?
You are writing a card for your boyfriend's birthday. His roommates will almost certainly see it on the counter. Do you write it the way you feel, or do you keep it neutral?

You have been offered a job in another city that would be a significant step up in your career. Your boyfriend of eighteen months has a job he loves where you currently live. What do you think about, and what do you do?
You are at a bar with a group of friends when a stranger approaches and starts flirting with you, assuming you are straight. He is harmless but persistent. How do you handle it?

Your best friend from childhood is getting married and has asked you to bring a plus-one. You have been seeing someone for two months and it feels right, but the wedding will be full of people from your hometown who knew you before you came out. Do you bring him?
I've been out to my friends for years but not to my parents. My boyfriend wants to meet them and I keep putting it off. He's starting to take it personally. What would you tell me to do?

You are at a company retreat and everyone is sharing a bit about their personal lives over dinner. The conversation turns to partners and families. Most of your colleagues do not know you are gay. What do you share?
You match with someone online who is significantly more out and publicly visible about his identity than you are comfortable being right now. He seems great. Do you keep talking to him?

Your landlord has put a clause in the new lease renewal that bans 'unregistered overnight guests.' You and your boyfriend regularly spend nights at each other's places. Do you sign, push back, or look for a new place?
You are at a family dinner and your uncle makes a joke that uses a slur. Everyone laughs uncomfortably. Your partner is sitting next to you. What do you do?

I came out to my best friend last year and she was supportive, but lately she keeps making comments about how she 'doesn't see why it has to be such a big part of my identity.' It's starting to wear on me. What would you say to her?
A man you have been dating for four months tells you he has not come out to his family and is not sure he ever will. You have been out for years. How does that land, and what do you do with it?

You are writing your dating profile. You can set it so only men who have already indicated they are looking for men will see it, which limits your reach, or you can make it visible to everyone, which means fielding a lot of mismatched messages. Which do you choose and why?

Your employer announces a new workplace wellness program that includes a couples' retreat. The sign-up form has checkboxes for 'employee and wife' or 'employee and husband' and nothing else. You want to bring your boyfriend. What do you do?
A man you have had feelings for a long time tells you he thinks he might be into men but is not sure. He asks what you think he should do. What do you say?

You are traveling internationally for work and you learn that the country you are visiting criminalizes same-sex relationships. You are expected to attend dinners and social events. How do you think about and prepare for the trip?

You are asked by your company to represent them at an industry conference. You discover the conference is sponsored in part by an organization that actively lobbies against rights for people like you. Do you go?

I've been with my partner for five years and we've talked about getting married, but neither of our families has fully accepted the relationship. He wants to do a big wedding; I'm not sure I want to put us through that. What do you think I should do?

You are out with a man you have been seeing for six weeks and he reaches for your hand while you are walking through a neighborhood you do not know well. You notice a group of men ahead who are watching you. What do you do?
A friend asks you to be honest about whether you think his new girlfriend is right for him. You genuinely do not think she treats him well. He seems happy. What do you say?

You are considering adopting a dog and the rescue organization requires a home visit. The volunteer who comes is friendly but asks several times whether there is 'a woman in the house' to help with care. How do you handle the conversation?

You have been invited to your boyfriend's high school reunion. He has not seen most of these people in ten years and is nervous about how they will react to seeing him arrive with a man. He asks what you think he should do. What do you tell him?
